ledger.note: 1377: the Berau kingdom begins. 'Kerajaan ini berdiri pada abad ke-14' with the first ruler Baddit Dipattung, 'Aji Raden Suryanata Kesuma/ Baddit Dipatung (1377-1401)'; the infobox span is 1377-1810. The page gives the century and the first reign, not a founding day.

1731: Bulungan becomes Berau's vassal. 'Bulungan was recognised as a vassal of the sultan of Berau, the latter acknowledging himself a vassal of Kutai' (Wira Amir's reign; infobox 'Vassal of the Sultanate of Berau (1731-1789)').

1789: Bulungan breaks away. 'After the civil war in Berau, Sulu sacked both Berau and Tarakan in 1789,' and 'Bulungan declared independence from Berau' (the second sentence has no year of its own; Berau 'fell under a civil war in 1770').

wars.name: Sulu sack of Berau and Tarakan
wars.outcome: Sulu sacked Berau and Tarakan; Bulungan declared independence from Berau. No Sulu occupation of land is recorded.
wars.note: The Indonesian Berau page has no 1789 sentence; its only Sulu line is 'kemudian ditaklukan Sultan Sulu' about Tidung, undated.

certainty.note: Both pages give no boundary; the sultanate is a coastal strip and river basins in forest, with Bulungan, Kutai and Tidung lands beside it.

notes: Written 2026-10-24 by the se-03-x additions batch, at the request of the se-03-a notes (Berau as suzerain of Bulungan 1731-1789). Two pages opened. Unsettled: (1) the overlord of Berau: the English Bulungan page says Berau 'acknowledg[ed] himself a vassal of Kutai' (1731 context), the Indonesian Berau page calls it a former dependency of the 'negara Banjar Raya' and says the 4 May 1826 treaty gave 'vazal-vazal Banjar termasuk negeri Berau' to the Dutch; no event is recorded for either (the vassal's side is for the kutai-kingdom and sultanate-of-banjar dossiers; the vassal events here are Berau's own, as suzerain of Bulungan, in the schema's convention, and the Bulungan dossier carries the mirror under the string 'Berau Sultanate'); (2) the year of the division into Gunung Tabur and Sambaliung: the Indonesian page gives no year, the infobox ends Berau in 1810, the Sambaliung dossier uses c. 1810; (3) the Bulungan page says the Dutch conquered Berau in 1834 and signed an agreement on 27 September, which is after Berau's end here: that is the two successors (sultanate-of-sambaliung, and Gunung Tabur, which needs a dossier); (4) the page's territory runs to the Kinabatangan, far beyond the outline drawn; (5) capital coordinates approximate; (6) rulers not recorded (the page has a list; only its first and last entries were read); (7) the id.wikipedia page is the only page for Berau opened: the English title does not exist. Gazetteer names: Berau, Tanjung Redeb, Sungai Lati, Tarakan (place or region), Tanjung Mangkalihat.
